title: Operations Manager Salary: How to Convert Hourly Rates to Annual Pay
description: Understand the operations manager salary landscape. Learn how to convert hourly rates to annual, fortnightly, and weekly pay using 38-hour weeks, tax, and super.
salarySummary: Operations manager salaries vary widely, but using the ABS average full-time adult ordinary time earnings of $2,083.70 per week (about $54.83 per hour for 38 hours) provides a useful benchmark.

faqs.q: What is the typical operations manager salary in Australia?
faqs.a: There is no single award rate for operations managers because the role spans many industries. The ABS Average Weekly Earnings for full-time adult ordinary time employees was $2,083.70 per week in May 2026, which equates to about $54.83 per hour for a 38-hour week. Many operations managers earn above this average, but the exact figure depends on the industry, experience, and whether an enterprise agreement or individual contract applies.

faqs.q: How do I convert an hourly operations manager rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply the hourly rate by the number of hours worked per week, then by 52. For a standard full-time role, assume 38 hours per week. For example, $60 per hour × 38 hours × 52 weeks = $118,560 per year. This calculation assumes the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. Use the [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) guide for more details.

faqs.q: Does superannuation and tax affect my operations manager salary calculations?
faqs.a: Yes. Superannuation guarantee is 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top of your salary, up to the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is calculated using the 2026–27 resident tax scale: nil up to $18,200, then 15% to $45,000, 30% to $135,000, 37% to $190,000, and 45% above that. Medicare levy generally adds 2%. For an estimate of your take-home pay, see the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Operations Manager Salary Landscape

When evaluating an **operations manager salary**, it is important to distinguish between award-covered roles, enterprise agreements, and individual contracts. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides [pay guides](/blog) for many awards that may cover operations managers in industries such as manufacturing, transport, or professional services. However, many operations managers are not covered by a specific award classification and instead have their pay set by agreement or contract.

For a broad benchmark, the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) Average Weekly Earnings for full-time adult ordinary time employees was $2,083.70 per week in May 2026. Dividing by 38 hours gives an average hourly rate of approximately $54.83. This is a useful reference point, but actual operations manager salaries can range from below this average in junior roles to well above it in senior positions.

### How to Convert an Hourly Rate to an Annual Salary

The standard formula for converting an hourly rate to an annual salary is:

**Annual gross = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For full-time work, we assume 38 hours per week, as set by the National Employment Standards. For example:

- $55 per hour × 38 hours × 52 weeks = $108,680 per year
- $70 per hour × 38 hours × 52 weeks = $138,320 per year

You can also calculate fortnightly pay by multiplying the weekly amount by 2. Weekly pay is hourly rate × 38. For $55 per hour, weekly pay is $2,090, and fortnightly pay is $4,180.

This calculation assumes the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. If you work more than 38 hours regularly, your actual annual pay may be higher, but overtime may be unpaid if you are a salaried manager.

### The Role of Awards and the National Minimum Wage

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours, as set by the Fair Work Commission. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making the casual rate $33.05 per hour. This is the legal minimum for award/agreement-free adult employees. Operations managers almost always earn well above this minimum.

If you are covered by an award, the award may specify a classification for operations manager or a similar role. Check the relevant [pay guides](/blog) from the Fair Work Ombudsman to find the correct minimum rate for your industry. For example, the Professional Employees Award or the Manufacturing Award may have classifications that apply. If you are not covered by an award, your employer must pay at least the National Minimum Wage.

### Tax and Superannuation Considerations

Your annual gross salary is the starting point for tax and super. The Australian Taxation Office (ATO) sets the 2026–27 resident tax rates:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% of excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: $4,020 plus 30% of excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: $31,020 plus 37% of excess over $135,000
- $190,001+: $51,420 plus 45% of excess over $190,000

Medicare levy generally adds 2% of taxable income. The 2025–26 single reduction thresholds are used here because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed at the time of this estimate.

Superannuation guarantee is 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top of your salary. For an operations manager earning $120,000 per year, the employer must contribute an additional $14,400 in super, up to the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Super is not deducted from your salary; it is an extra cost for the employer.

### Using the Timesheet Calculator

Our [timesheet](/) tool lets you enter your base hourly rate and optionally add 25% casual loading. It then calculates your weekly, fortnightly, and annual gross pay, along with estimated tax and super. Remember: if you are a permanent employee, your rate already includes any loading for casual work. Do not add casual loading unless you are genuinely a casual employee.

For operations managers, the timesheet calculator is a quick way to see how your hourly rate translates into annual figures. You can also use the [reference tables](/data) to compare your pay with award rates or average earnings.

### Summary

An operations manager salary is best understood by converting the hourly rate to annual using 38 hours per week and 52 weeks. The ABS average full-time earnings provide a benchmark, but your actual pay depends on your industry, experience, and agreement. Always check the relevant award or agreement for minimum entitlements, and remember that super is paid on top of your salary. For a personalised estimate, use the [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) guide or the timesheet calculator.
